title: hosted/dedicated replay deduplication bug + customer escalation runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a high-severity customer escalation, a recurring pattern of 5xx and timeouts was observed when requests routed from Dedicated pools to Hosted fallbacks. The root cause investigation shows idempotency token collisions and header rewrite at the Dedicated->Hosted edge bridge that allowed duplicate inflight executions, thrashing KV caches and saturating worker queues. This ticket tracks the short-term hotfix, the medium-term architectural mitigation (tenant-scoped replay limiter + token normalization), and customer-facing escalation/runbook artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Edge proxy normalizes inbound idempotency header and preserves original client token across Dedicated->Hosted bridge
Tenant-scoped replay limiter prevents >1 concurrent in-flight request per idempotency token per tenant for bridge-qualified requests
No repeat 5xx waves for affected tenant(s) for 72 hours after rollout
Automated e2e test added in integration suite that simulates bridge replay and asserts single execution
Customer escalation email template and status page snippet published and linked in ticket
investigation_notes: 2026-03-01 09:14 — Pagerood: Several customers reported elevated 502/504 and timeouts; spike correlated with cross-mode routing when Dedicated capacity hit autoscale limits
Trace sampling shows duplicate request traces with different edge request IDs but identical client idempotency header values — suggests header rewrite or collision at proxy layer
KV cache metrics show eviction spikes coincident with duplicated executions; runtime worker queue depth rose 4x leading to request timeouts
Affected flow: Dedicated bridge -> frontdoor translator -> hosted inference runtime; rollback to serving-local success observed when requests pinned to Dedicated without bridge
Hypothesis: Some proxies were injecting their own idempotency token or normalizing whitespace/case causing token aliasing across concurrent requests
steps_taken: 2026-03-01 10:00 — Immediate mitigation: Enabled conservative admission control on Dedicated bridge to limit burst fanout to Hosted (config toggle: bridge.max_fanout=2)
2026-03-01 12:30 — Telemetry: Added high-sample tracing on bridge to capture raw idempotency header, edge rewrite logs, and original-client-ip for affected tenants
2026-03-02 02:15 — Hotfix deployed: Edge shim normalizes idempotency header (trims whitespace, preserves case) and marks canonical-token in x-rw-canonical-idempotency header
2026-03-03 08:40 — Observed initial reduction in duplicate traces; worker queue depth fell ~60% for the impacted pools
2026-03-04 16:00 — Canary rollout of tenant-scoped replay limiter at edge (config: replay_limiter.per_tenant=true, max_concurrent_per_token=1) to 10% of traffic for affected region
decisions: Implement normalization and replay-limiter at the bridge/edge instead of requiring SDK changes — rationale: immediate cross-cutting impact reduction without forcing customers to update clients
Use tenant-scoped limiter (per-tenant keyspace) rather than global limiter to avoid cross-tenant throttling and preserve fairness
Short-term fix implemented as config flags and a small shim in the bridge; long-term plan is to bake dedup semantics into the bridge runtime (requires migration schedule)
We will not change idempotency semantics of existing endpoints; we only canonicalize token representation and enforce single-concurrency per canonical token for bridge-routed requests
blockers: Need production infra migration window for persistent token canonicalization (infra scheduling with SRE)
Edge config rollout requires signed-off deployment plan from Networking and SRE teams
Dependency: dedicated-bridge library update must be backward-compatible with older Dedicated host versions used by some enterprise customers
prs: GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bridge/pull/1427 — edge: idempotency canonicalization shim
GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bridge/pull/1431 — tenant-scoped replay limiter and metrics
GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/981 — integration test for deduplication flow
playbook_snippet: If tenant reports 5xx during Dedicated->Hosted fallback: 1) Enable bridge.max_fanout=1 for affected tenant, 2) Turn on bridge.replay_limiter.per_tenant for region, 3) Enable high-sample tracing for idempotency headers, 4) Communicate to customer with templated message and ETA for fix
next_steps: Complete code review and merge PRs for canonicalization and replay limiter (owners: @diego, @mariaS)
Schedule infra migration window with SRE to make canonical token persistent (requires DB schema update) — owner: SRE
Add synthetic test in nightly pipeline to simulate bridge replay scenarios and assert single execution
Follow up with Solutions Engineering to notify affected customers and provide mitigation guidance and status updates
Write postmortem and include recommended SLA/observability enhancements in runtime-1.22 planning
